newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvian minister says to pursue sell-offs.
newsitem.headline: Latvian minister says to pursue sell-offs.

text.p: Latvian Economy Minister Guntar Krasts on Wednesday said that the Baltic state would push on with the privatisation of state-owned companies.
He also forecast a rise in gross domestic product (GDP) this year of 3.5-5.0 percent.

"We plan to privatise (electricity company) Latvenergo this year, restructure Latvian Gas and continue the sell-off process," Krasts said in a speech before a seminar at the Latvian bourse on capital markets.
"We hope to thus release more credit resources by the end of this year," Krasts added.
Privatisation in Latvia has received a boost under Prime Minister Andris Shkele with many key companies coming up for sale, including the gas company and the state shipping firm.
He said the GDP rise would come amid falling inflation and lower interest rates. The forecast is in line with previous government expectations for growth this year.
Krasts said that the government would try to boost exports by creating a credit guarantee agency with the support of the European Union (EU) PHARE programme.
Krasts also said that Latvia would continue bringing its domestic market up to EU standards.
